notes.text: Today's Done and Upcoming no longer jump when you open a todo or go back to the list.
Work tags show their website's icon for more sites, including ones with long home pages.
The account picture at the top of the list sits in a round button, matching the + beside it.

You can now change who a card goes to before you send it: add or remove recipients, Cc and Bcc, edit a new email's subject or the account it's sent from, and pick a different Slack channel or person. You can @-mention people in a Slack message's words.
The Done button on the notes toolbar sits at the right end of the bar again.
None on its own: users see this with the next PR's controls.
Signing in to a website now has back, forward and reload, and lets you switch to a window the site opened, like "Continue with Google".
Every card in a task's thread now opens with the app or site it goes through and who it goes to.
Cards in a task's thread share one look on each app, and confirming on a website says exactly which button it presses. iPhone: a text waiting for your Mac can be discarded from the phone.
Connecting Messages now asks for permission to send texts during setup, and sending a text asks for it first if needed, instead of failing.

Sign-in sheets now follow "Continue with Google" and other sign-in windows a site opens. Mac: The sign-in sheet shows the site's page at full size, with the site's address in the header and a Cancel button beside I'm done. The sign-in card explains why it needs you in one short line.
Today, Calendar, Asks and Chat are tabs in the system's tab bar, and a task opens inside the tab you opened it from.
Tap a task's icons to see everyone and everything on it, and open any of them.
The work a task is for shows its icon among the task's other icons.
A work's or person's page shows their name and picture in the bar.
Add a todo from the + at the top right of Today and the Calendar, with its day, priority, dictation and photos or files.
Opening a long brief continues where you were reading.
A call with Augmenter shows in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen, where you can mute it or hang up.
Faces show in full colour whether or not someone is on Augmenter.
Chat is last on the rail, after Asks, and ⌘4 opens it.
A worker can now book or buy on a website for you: it shows you exactly what it's about to do, and does it only after you confirm.
Work tags show their website's icon far more often: Augmenter now learns a job's website from the addresses of the people you work with there.
A worker browsing a website for you recognizes buttons that would buy, book or send on any site, not only ones using familiar words, and leaves them for you to confirm.
A worker can browse websites for your tasks again.
A street address in a task's brief is a Google Maps link, so one tap gives directions.

A worker can now search a booking site for you (dates, party size, times) to find what's available, and never books or buys anything itself. A worker can read a site's subdomains, such as a payment or account page, not just its main address.
A worker can now look things up in each account you've connected, including your GitHub pull requests and issues, and cites what it read in the task's brief.
A worker can now post a Slack message or thread reply for you, as you, once you approve its card; reconnect Slack to allow it.
When you have more than one Gmail connected, a new email your worker drafts says which address it's from, picked for the task, and is sent from that address.
Addresses in a task's brief link to Google Maps, so one tap gives directions.
On the calendar, a snoozed task now shows on the day it comes back rather than its original day.
A task's worker can now send a new email from your Gmail, once you approve it, to someone you name.
People's faces on tasks no longer include websites, products or teams, and a link in a task's title no longer puts a face on it.
Snoozed tasks now sit under Upcoming on Today, alongside what is due later, and tasks snoozed to Someday live under Later on the calendar.
Every change listed in What's new and the changelog starts with a capital letter.
A task's worker now asks its questions on a card you answer with a tap: pick an option, pick several, or write your own.
A task's worker now knows which accounts you've connected, and asks you to reconnect one rather than drafting something it can't send.
A task's worker can read websites again.
A worker whose draft could not be saved no longer leaves the task in Needs you with nothing to send; it says what happened instead.
Done now sits above Snoozed on Today and starts open, so what you finished today is in view.
a message card opened by resting on a source in a task's notes no longer closes by itself while the task's details load.

Rows and open todos show the people they are about first, as faces on their tool logos, with a +N when there are more. Companies, bots, notification senders and your own other addresses no longer show up as people. Mac: people you text show the picture on their Contacts card.
Connections now has two tabs: Connected, for the apps and websites Augmenter can use for you, and Library, for what you can add, including signing in to any website.
an edit made just as your network drops no longer disappears from the list until you're back online.
You can attach photos and files to a task's thread, from the paperclip on the Mac and the + on the iPhone.
Connecting Messages or WhatsApp now finishes on its own after you turn on Full Disk Access and reopen Augmenter.
A drafted text or WhatsApp message now always goes to the person's conversation or their number, never just their name.
Outlook is no longer available as a connection.
The worker's sign-in card shows the site's icon.
Each day on the calendar is wider, so todos have more room for their titles.
Work tags on a task show the work's website icon; on the Mac, a narrow window shows just the icon.
A snoozed task shows how long until it comes back, like 3h or 2d. Mac: Tasks shown in chat now show the same icons and details as on your list.
A task you finish from its worker chat stays under today's Done, even when it was overdue.
Augmenter waits until you've finished writing a task's notes before its worker starts drafting. Rewriting your notes, or asking for changes, gets you a new draft that replaces the old one.
Augmenter no longer jumps in front of the app you're using when you press a ⌃⌥ shortcut with another key, such as ⌃⌥⌘ window shortcuts or a hyper key.
A message to a task's worker that fails to send is no longer lost; it stays in the composer with the error.
Every task now has its own worker you can message from the task's page, and Send on a worker's draft sends it.
When you ask someone for something in a connected tool, it lands in Asks with their face and closes when it arrives.
Tell the assistant "I asked Sarah for the deck by Friday" and it tracks it in Asks.
Asks, a tab after Chat, lists what you're waiting on other people for, each with the face of whoever has it.
Todos show the people they involve, in colour when they're on Augmenter.
Asks, a tab after Chat (⌘4), lists what you're waiting on other people for, each with the face of whoever has it; hover a face to see when you asked.
Todos show the people they involve, in colour when they're on Augmenter.
When someone on Augmenter has the todo you asked them for, your ask follows their progress and closes when they finish.
Today is one list by status on the Mac and the iPhone; sections are gone, and what you wrote in them is kept as your work.
Setup steps (Connect Slack, Gmail and the rest) sit first among your todos, with no Setup heading.
Augmenter files each todo under the work it belongs to, instead of a section.
The arrow keys move between setup steps and todos in both directions.
A task shows the work it belongs to and the people it's with; click one to see everything for it.
A task shows the work it belongs to and the people it's with; tap one to see everything for it.
A task can have a worker: its thread with the worker sits under the brief, and you can message it. While it works you see it typing, then its reply.
Every open task has a box at the foot of its page to message about it; writing there gets its worker going, and a task's thread appears once either of you has written.
While a worker is working on a task you see it typing, and you can stop it from the same box.
Your message leaves the composer the moment you send it.
Tell a task's worker "I've got it" and it steps back; ask it to change your list or rename the task and it will.
A task a worker is working on shows a turning mark on its row.
A list of items you give a task becomes a checklist, and keeps that form as items are added.
Workers take on more of your tasks: an appointment, a call or a conversation gets one to find the place, check the details or draft what to say. Shopping lists, chores and short reminders stay yours.
A task's worker keeps its brief short and current, rewriting it rather than adding to it, and leaves your own notes as you wrote them.
A worker's draft shows as a card in the task's thread: edit its words, then Send or Discard, and the card says whether it went.
When you send or discard a worker's draft, the worker learns what happened and closes the task or takes the next step.
A reply a worker drafts can be sent from your Gmail, in the thread it answers, when you press Send. Connecting Gmail now also asks to send the replies you approve.
A worker can read websites for its task, and asks you to sign in to a site when it needs to, carrying on once you have.
A todo's day comes from your words, and adding a todo never moves it into another section.
Press R on a task's page to message its worker.
Press ⌘↵ to send a draft on a task's page.
The texts and WhatsApp messages you approve are sent from your Mac, even ones you approved on your phone.
The I key and the rail's "I'll handle it" are gone.
The action rail beside a task's page is gone, and the card keeps the window's width; S or 9 opens Snooze under the page's ⋯, and the other keys work as before.
The floating composer is gone: add todos in Today's "Add todo" rows, and ask Augmenter in the Chat tab, which / opens from anywhere.
A single ⌃⌥ puts the caret in Today's add row, or in Chat its composer; N goes to the add row.
Tap a draft to edit it full screen, then send it.
Sign in to a website for your worker with the iPhone keyboard, passwords and codes filled in as in Safari.

A bell at the top right counts the tasks that need you. Tap it to go through them as cards over your list: swipe left to snooze one (with Undo), right to act on it, or tap to open it; pull down or tap the bell to put them away.
Today has an "Add todo" row at the end of the list, with dictation, and the composer now lives in the Chat tab.
What you share into Augmenter fills Today's add row, or with an image opens the Chat tab.

Marking a task done or snoozing it keeps your place, so the next task is selected and you can keep working down the list. Tasks you're doing stay in your list on Today, in your order, instead of a separate Doing group.
New installations check for the latest update before opening, and releases without native changes arrive over the air without requiring a new TestFlight build.

An open task has its actions down the right (Done, I'll handle it, Snooze, Send to agent, Drop, Delete), and ↑ and ↓ step to the next task. Mac: Press S to snooze a todo, picking from a menu of times that each show when the todo comes back. Mac: Shortcut hints are capitalized, and a task's status picker shows each status's key. Mac: On Today, the groups open one at a time, the arrow keys step into the group below or above, and an open task stays open. iPhone: An open task has Done, I'll handle it, Snooze and Drop along its foot, and Snooze shows when each option brings it back. iPhone: On Today, the groups open one at a time. Later is now called Snooze on the Mac and iPhone.
The composer's mic now dictates what you say into the field as you speak, for you to edit and send.

Call Augmenter from the Chat tab: what you say shows as you say it, both sides of the call stay in the conversation as ordinary messages with the todos an answer is about, the todo it is about opens beside the chat, and a red pill at the top of the window ends the call when the chat is out of view. iPhone: Call Augmenter from the Chat tab: what you say shows as you say it, both sides of the call stay in the conversation as ordinary messages with the todos an answer is about, the call carries on as you switch tabs, and a red button at the top ends it. iPhone: The microphone permission now says it is for dictation and calls.
The home page's "Hand off the easy stuff." scene keeps Claude and ChatGPT fully on screen on narrower windows.

Chat is now its own tab on the Mac and iPhone: one conversation with Augmenter that follows you between devices, shows the todos it makes or mentions as rows you can open, answers in friendly full sentences, and keeps a history of your earlier chats, and shows Augmenter typing while it works rather than every step it takes; on the Mac, the arrow keys and a right-click work on those todos just as they do on your list.
When someone tells you to take your time on something, its todo no longer stays due or says it is overdue.
Clicking anywhere in an Add todo row now puts the cursor in it.
A shopping list you text someone now becomes one todo named for the trip, with the items as a checklist in its notes.
set a todo's priority with ⌥1, ⌥2 or ⌥3, and clear it with ⌥0.
A call or meeting you set up by text now goes on the todo you already have for talking with that person, instead of a second one.
On computers without a graphics card, augmenter.com now shows its painted picture instead of freezing for several seconds while it loads.
Today shows what's open first, with Doing, Snoozed, Done and Upcoming collapsed beneath it, and Later now snoozes a todo until a time you pick without changing its due date.
Today shows what's open first, with Doing, Snoozed, Done and Upcoming collapsed beneath it, and Later now snoozes a todo until a time you pick without changing its due date.
The home page now shows the lounge chair and fig beneath the triptych, spreads the app logos evenly round the notebook without Outlook, and lights up One World Trade and the skyline at night.
The composer's button is a voice button when empty and turns into a blue send as you type; on the Mac, a longer message keeps its buttons in a row beneath.
Headings read calmer, in a lighter weight with normal letter spacing.
The home page now turns to face the terrace doors and walks out through them, and a reading lamp lights the library corner at night.
The home page is now a cast-iron loft in lower Manhattan, by day and by night, with a switch for light or dark.
Today by status has an Add todo row again, under what's still open.

Today can be organized by status (the new default), with what needs you first, or by section, from the toggle beside the date; your choice follows you to every device. The calendar now lists each day by status, most recently edited first.
Connecting a tool now brings in the last two weeks of messages instead of one.
Tables in a pull request's description now show as tables in its card, instead of rows of pipes.
Texts containing emoji no longer stop Messages, WhatsApp or Telegram from syncing.
The privacy policy now explains that product analytics include what you do and write in Augmenter, while what your connections bring in stays out unless you choose to contribute it.
Connect Outlook: Augmenter reads your Focused inbox and the conversations you reply in from a Microsoft work, school or personal account, to find tasks and keep them up to date.
Simple voice requests, like adding or moving a todo, get answered faster.
Notifications no longer show raw card markup like `<GitHubPullRequest>` in place of the todo's description.
Voice waits for you to finish, stops talking when you say "wait", and no longer acts on a half-finished request or rearranges your whole list without asking.
Voice conversations are kept like typed chats again.
A todo's brief links a shared document directly, so it opens in one step.
When a message changes a todo, its brief is rewritten to include it within a minute, with the message linked in the sentence it backs, instead of a separate line left at the bottom.
A todo's brief links straight to a document someone shared, not to the message they shared it in.
The Connect and Open in buttons at the bottom of a sheet now sit lower, in line with the composer.
A source's logo in a todo's notes now stays on the same line as its words.
Badge updates no longer cause repeated notification processing.
See what changed across Augmenter at augmenter.com/changelog.
After an update, What's new shows what changed since you last opened the app.
Connections opens as a sheet, with Connect at the foot of each tool's page.
Each item in a todo's menus has an icon beside it.
A source's hover card stays whole and in view, and its messages scroll.
A message that was only an image now shows the image on its own.
The blue dot and badge now mark only new todos, not updates.
Coding agents can now manage sections, tags, order, undo and connections through Augmenter.
Only the agent that takes on a pasted todo links itself to it.
Briefs cite their sources inline, in a few words of the sentence each backs.
Hover a citation to see its message; click to open it.
Tap a citation to see its message in a sheet.
Connect Wispr Flow so action items from its meeting notes become todos.
Ask what needs you and the assistant starts with todos at Needs you.
Once you're let in, the waitlist screen opens straight into the app.
After connecting a tool in the browser, you're brought back to the app.
Emoji codes in GitHub and Slack cards draw as emoji.
Open TestFlight on the update screen goes straight to Augmenter's page.
Scrolling over a card in a brief carries on into the notes past its end.
Connect Telegram.
Lines you add below a brief are kept as you wrote them.
Connect WhatsApp.
Needs you, a new status, marks todos where the next move is yours.
Opening a todo no longer makes its notes jump as source cards load.
Source cards in a brief always draw as cards, never as raw text.
Opening a pull request for a todo moves it to Doing, and its card shows Merged once it merges.
The Gmail connection page explains what's read and how it's used before you connect.
Inviting people from the app has been removed.
Todos are filed into sections as they're written; nothing reshuffles them later.
Check off a todo and a line sweeps through it.
A coding agent shows on a todo only once it starts working on it.
A Slack rate limit no longer stalls syncing your connections.
Briefs say what the work is, without guessed checklists of steps.
Coding agents keep a todo's notes to one short, current status.
A coding agent's logo sits with a todo's tool logos and no longer pulses.
Invite and Feedback open as standard sheets, and the account menu matches the Mac's icons.
The app opens onto your list on a slow network, not a blank screen.
A todo's title scrolls away with its notes and fades into the bar.
A blue dot marks todos that changed while you were away.
Sharing into Augmenter fills the composer, so you can edit before sending.
Copy a todo as markdown with ⇧⌘C.
The row highlight settles on its row without bouncing past it.
The assistant can edit notes that show a texts card.
A todo shows a logo for every tool its notes draw on, overlapping.
Todos you type or edit are briefed shortly after.
Your ✅ on a Slack message shows as a reaction in its card, not a message from you.
Copied or shared todos end with the same agent instructions Send to includes.
A todo is briefed from its own section's work, never another project's with similar words.
The feedback button's tooltip shows its shortcut, ⌘⇧F.
Spacing and alignment are tidier across dialogs, menus and the list.
The highlight slides from row to row as you move through the list.
GitHub pull requests and issues show as cards in briefs.
Your merged pull requests now reliably close the todos they finish.
A todo only to attend an event closes once the event has passed.
Send to reopens a todo's agent thread when it already has one.
A todo typed before your list finishes loading is kept, not lost.
A closed todo no longer shows its agent as still working.
The highlighted row stands out more clearly in light mode.
Emails in briefs read the way your mail app shows them, without template clutter.
The ChatGPT and Claude connection pages explain how they work on your todos.
Todos finished in another conversation now close on their own.
Connect GitHub, and a merged pull request closes the todo it ships.
A message from any connection can now update or close a todo another one made.
Every new todo, including ones you type, gets a researched brief.
Send to opens ChatGPT or Claude on the todo's brief, ready to edit before sending.
With nothing selected, ⌘C copies the todo in front of you as markdown.
Connect ChatGPT or Claude from Connections.
Press ⇧⌘↩ to send a todo to the agent you used last.
Invitations come back every Monday, and Invite shows each one's status.
Copy a todo as markdown, with its quoted messages, from its menu.
Share a todo as markdown from its menu.
Send a todo to ChatGPT or Claude, which can work on it through Augmenter.
The calendar's heading names a single month and year.
Press ⌘⇧F anywhere to send feedback.
Feedback and Invite open as dialogs over the window.
Feedback, Invite and Connections slide up from the bottom; swipe down to close.
Updates apply as you leave the app, without needing a fresh launch.
The composer's placeholder sits centred in its field.
Send feedback with a screenshot or file, then book a call with us right after.
A text from a business about your own account, like a failed payment, now becomes a todo.
